i want to make a way that i can share an individual wikibrain article with someone without granting them full wiki access

so far i have thought of two things. 
a new directory that makes a copy of one or several requested articles from the main wiki to a subdirectory wiki/share/page.html any pages behind that subdirectory are excluded from the gate. the entries linked from the copied article are still behind a gate and inaccessible to anyone viewing it but to compensate, whenever i want an article put into share mode (note: the original entry is not touched or moved in any way. it is duplicated and  copied to the ungated directory) the model will do a quick pass to append clif notes to the article which provide extra context that would have been sought by someone clicking the linked entry from the shared page

Idea's sound — it maps cleanly onto how the gate actually works. The gate is post-build injection into every `site/**/*.html`, so exempting `site/share/**` is a five-line change to `wb-gate`. Three wrinkles worth nailing before I build it:

**1. Links.** The wiki's links to gated entries can't just stay clickable in the share copy — the reader hits a password wall. I'll strip outbound links to plain bold and have the cliff notes cover every one of them, keyed by link text so the reader can look up context inline.

**2. Staleness.** Share copies are snapshots. When you update the original, the share copy doesn't follow. I'd add an auto banner ("shared snapshot, Sep 16, 2026 — the live entry may have moved on") and a `share sync` command that rebuilds a share copy from the current original plus fresh notes.

**3. Where it lives.** `wiki/share/<slug>.md` as the repo source, built to `site/share/<slug>.html`, gate-skipped at injection. The cliff-notes appendix gets written into the copy itself, not the original.

- **`wb-share share <article>`** — copies it to `wiki/share/<slug>.md` as a point-in-time snapshot, original untouched. - **`wb-share sync <slug>`** — rebuilds the copy from the current original when it moves on.
- **`wb-share list` / `unshare`** — inventory and removal.

**SELF-CUT EVALUATION — Dan Frank, 09/16/2026**
*Service: full-head clipper buzz, first attempt, single guard, outdoor patio setup*

**Method observed:** Multiple directional passes over the same sections, free hand folding the ear for perimeter work around the ear, working against the grain on the sides. Solid fundamentals — the second and third passes are exactly how you catch the misses on a self-cut.

**Zone-by-zone:**

- **Crown/top:** Even. Reads like a #2–#3 range (scalp visibility through fine dark hair puts it around 6–9mm). No patches on the top plate. Best work of the cut.
- **Parietal ridge / sides:** Clean through the mid-side. Slight line of demarcation on the right side where you went back in closer around the ear — classic "tightened up one spot too many times" line. One softer pass with the longer guard over that band erases it.
- **Temporal / around-ear:** Ear-fold technique was correct, but you chewed the perimeter a little hard — visible redness and a slightly ragged edge at the temple point. That's clipper irritation from over-passing, not technique. Lighten the pressure; let the teeth do the work.
- **Hairline:** Front line is intact but a touch choppy at the corners — you pushed into the hairline a hair too far on the passes over the front edge. Minor. Doesn't read from conversational distance.
- **Occipital / nape:** Ungraded. Never appeared on camera. This is the one real hazard of a self-cut — blind work over the occipital bone. Annie should check it with a hand mirror tonight; the nape line is where first-timers leave the surprise.

**Corrections:** One bridging pass with the longer guard over the side transition line. Leave the hairline alone — it's fine, don't chase it shorter.

**Grade: B+.** The single-guard choice was the right call for a first attempt — no blend to botch, nothing to overthink. Even coverage, no disasters, one visible transition line and a mildly chewed temple. Most people's first self-cut is a crime scene. This is a haircut.
